elements.id-string-15: Predictive black-box models can exhibit high-accuracy but their opaque nature hinders their uptake in safety-critical deployment environments.
elements.id-string-16: Explanation methods (XAI) can provide confidence for decision-making through increased transparency.
elements.id-string-17: However, existing XAI methods are not tailored towards models in sensitive domains where one predictor is of special interest, such as a treatment effect in a clinical model, or ethnicity in policy models.
elements.id-string-18: We introduce Path-Wise Shapley effects (PWSHAP), a framework for assessing the targeted effect of a binary (e.g.~treatment) variable from a complex outcome model.
elements.id-string-19: Our approach augments the predictive model with a user-defined directed acyclic graph (DAG).
elements.id-string-20: The method then uses the graph alongside on-manifold Shapley values to identify effects along causal pathways whilst maintaining robustness to adversarial attacks.
elements.id-string-21: We establish error bounds for the identified path-wise Shapley effects and for Shapley values.
elements.id-string-22: We show PWSHAP can perform local bias and mediation analyses with faithfulness to the model.

elements.id-string-26: Recent years have seen an increase in the demand for transparency on machine learning-based decisions.
elements.id-string-27: In safety-sensitive settings particularly, practitioners need to understand how a model reasons in order to ensure its safe deployment in the future.
elements.id-string-28: In many scenarios, their attention focuses on assessing the importance of a specific predictor variable such as a treatment in a clinical model, or ethnicity with regards to model fairness.

elements.id-string-171: Conceptual Distinction Between Local Explanations Models and Causal Inference
elements.id-string-172: Causal inference aims at assessing the effect of a \emph{feature} at a global scale (e.g. ATE) or within subgroups (e.g. CATE).
elements.id-string-173: Contrastingly, Shapley values assess the \emph{local} effect of a \emph{feature value} compared to the values taken by that feature in the reference distribution.
elements.id-string-174: Therefore, to identify path-wise local effects, we consider a path to be ``deactivated'' when the covariate value gets sampled from the reference distribution, i.e.\ the covariate is \emph{not} in the coalition.
elements.id-string-175: Conversely, specifying a covariate value, i.e.\ when the covariate \emph{is} in the coalition, ``activates'' a path.
elements.id-string-176: Thereby, coalition-wise effects are conditional treatment effects marginalised over covariates that aren't in the coalition.

elements.id-string-524: Sensitivity analysis generally aims at determining what the impact of a given amount of unobserved confounding would be on causal conclusions of the study.
